sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page njan1240 'Njanga' (Hammarström et al.), with reference records 311970 (Robson 2011), 45692 (Connell 1998), 80761 (Griffiths & Robson 2010)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Catalogue only: 'Njanga, arguably a distinct language from Kwanja [knp], is missing from E16-E28'; AES nearly extinct; country listed as Nigeria (sources place Mbondjanga in Cameroon); three references, none typed phonology/grammar.

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce, Sascha S. Griffiths, Marieke Martin, Laura Robson & David Zeitlyn. 2021. Language ecology, language endangerment, and relict languages: Case studies from Adamawa (Cameroon-Nigeria). Open Linguistics 7: 244-300. doi:10.1515/opli-2021-0011 (CC-BY; Oxford ORA author copy)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 5 'Mbondjanga and the Kwanja Region: The Njanga Language' (pp. 270-278) covers geography, socio-economy, history, vitality, domains, internal variation and contact; the only linguistic remarks are that Robson 2011 compared a 1,628-word Njanga/Sundani corpus (76.3% cognate), found borrowings at 'lexical, phonological, and morphological' levels, and one definitive-marker example (/-ra/ Njanga, /-re/ Sundani). The words stress/accent never occur for Njanga; 'tonal' occurs only for Wawa and Somyev.

sources.citation: Weber, Joan & Martin Weber. 2008. Précis d'orthographe pour la langue kwanja (dialecte súndànɨ́). Ngaoundéré: EELC / Yaoundé: ANACLAC. 25 pp. (closest described relative; held under kwan1276)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress (a full-text search for stress/accent/stress/intensité: none). Describes Súndànɨ́ Kwanja as having 4 level lexical tones plus 8 contour tones (sec. 3, pp. 9-12); names only two Kwanja dialects (súndànɨ́ and ndùŋgánɨ̀), Njanga not mentioned. Not a description of Njanga.

sources.citation: AHRC project page 'Documentation of endangered languages and cultures in the Nigeria-Cameroon borderland' (Connell & Zeitlyn, University of Kent, 2006-2009), incl. Laura Robson's research profile. mambila.info/AHRC_Languages/
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; project description only (Robson to spend Aug 2007-2008 in Mbondjanga, c. 350 inhabitants, documenting Njanga, 'a dying language with less than 30 speakers'). No outputs or downloads listed.

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 1998. Moribund languages of the Nigeria-Cameroon borderland. In Matthias Brenzinger (ed.), Endangered languages in Africa, 207-225. Cologne: Rüdiger Köppe. (VIMS web version of the 1997 Leipzig symposium paper)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.3 'Njanga': spoken only in Mbondjanga, 'considered to be a dialect of Kwanja, but initial work shows it to be considerably different - apparently more conservative - than other Kwanja dialects'; spoken daily only by the chief and his notable; sec. 3 says the Njanga material 'has yet to be examined in detail'. No phonology, tone or stress.
